strings.name: Katie Ledecky
strings.summary: Ledecky emerged from American youth swimming and won Olympic 800m freestyle gold at fifteen in London. Pacing, endurance and years of training made her dominant in distance freestyle and brought repeated long-course world records. She finished Paris 2024 with nine golds and fourteen Olympic medals, broke the 800m record again in 2025 and continued competing internationally in 2026.
strings.coverageNote: Sources checked through 13 November 2026. Selected career milestones; results and records refer to their cited dates, not an exhaustive results log or live ranking.
strings.influence.rationale: An Olympic champion and distance freestyle world-record holder who redefined standards in women's endurance swimming.
strings.facts.fact-1.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.fact-2.label: University
strings.facts.fact-2.value: Stanford University; bachelor’s degree in psychology
strings.highlights.highlight-1.title: Gold across four Olympics
strings.highlights.highlight-1.text: Won the 800m freestyle at four successive Olympics from 2012 to 2024 and finished Paris with fourteen Olympic medals.
strings.highlights.highlight-2.title: Long-course 800m world record
strings.highlights.highlight-2.text: Swam 8:04.12 in Fort Lauderdale in May 2025, improving her own nearly nine-year-old long-course record.
strings.timeline.event-1.title: Pan Pacific 800m silver
strings.timeline.event-1.text: Finished second in Irvine in 8:07.26 behind Australia’s Lani Pallister.
strings.timeline.event-2.title: Seventh 800m world title
strings.timeline.event-2.text: Won the 800m freestyle in Singapore for her seventh world championship in the event.
strings.timeline.event-3.title: Improved the 800m long-course record
strings.timeline.event-3.text: Swam 8:04.12 in Fort Lauderdale, improving the record she set at Rio 2016.
strings.timeline.event-4.title: Nine Olympic golds after Paris
strings.timeline.event-4.text: Won the 800m and 1500m in Paris, bringing her Olympic total to nine golds, four silvers and one bronze.
strings.timeline.event-5.title: Moved her training to Florida
strings.timeline.event-5.text: Moved from Stanford to Gainesville to train with Anthony Nesty and joined Florida’s volunteer coaching staff.
strings.timeline.event-6.title: Two golds and two silvers in Tokyo
strings.timeline.event-6.text: Won the 800m and 1500m freestyle plus two silvers at the Tokyo Olympics held in 2021.
strings.timeline.event-7.title: 1500m record on her professional debut
strings.timeline.event-7.text: Swam 15:20.48 in Indianapolis in her first professional race, improving the long-course 1500m record.
strings.timeline.event-8.title: Four golds and a silver in Rio
strings.timeline.event-8.text: Won the 200m, 400m, 800m and a relay, setting world records in the 400m and 800m.
strings.timeline.event-9.title: Four golds at her first Worlds
strings.timeline.event-9.text: Won four gold medals in Barcelona and set world records in the 800m and 1500m freestyle.
strings.timeline.event-10.title: Olympic gold at fifteen
strings.timeline.event-10.text: Won the London Olympic 800m freestyle final at fifteen.
strings.timeline.event-11.title: Born in the Washington area
strings.timeline.event-11.text: Born in Washington, DC, grew up in Bethesda, Maryland, and began swimming at six.
